messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 62-year-old man presents to his primary care provider complaining of abdominal pain. He reports a 6-month history of gradually progressive epigastric pain and 10 pounds of unexpected weight loss. He has also noticed that his skin feels itchier than usual. His past medical history is notable for gout, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. He takes allopurinol, enalapril, and glyburide. He has a 10-pack-year smoking history and a distant history of cocaine abuse. His temperature is 100.1°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, and respirations are 20/min. On exam, he has notable hepatomegaly and a palpable gallbladder. A right upper quadrant ultrasound reveals an irregular extrahepatic mass originating from the gallbladder wall. Which of the following serum markers is most likely elevated in this patient?

Options:
A. Bombesin
B. CA-125
C. CA 19-9
D. S-100
E. Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase

Correct answer: C. CA 19-9

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "The question tests oncology knowledge (gallbladder cancer and its serum marker CA 19-9); the cocaine history is incidental and no psychiatric or DSM-5 content is involved."}
